article.title: Ubiquitous
article.description: Meaning: present, appearing, or found everywhere. Pronunciation: yoo-BIK-wi-tuhs. Example: 'Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern life.' Register: formal/academic, common in IELTS Writing Task 2 essays about technology or globalization.
article.content: Meaning: present, appearing, or found everywhere. Pronunciation: yoo-BIK-wi-tuhs. Example: 'Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern life.' Register: formal/academic, common in IELTS Writing Task 2 essays about technology or globalization.

generated.caption:
Ever wanted a more formal word for "everywhere"? 🤔 Meet **Ubiquitous**!

This powerful word means 'present, appearing, or found everywhere' and is perfect for IELTS Writing Task 2 essays. For example: 'Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern life.'

generated.script: Ye word ‘Ubiquitous’ sunke ya padhke confusion hota hai na? Toh aaj samjho! Okay, toh ‘Ubiquitous’ ka matlab hai jo cheez har jagah ho, sab jagah present ho, matlab found everywhere. Iska pronunciation hai yoo-BIK-wi-tuhs. Example: ‘Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern life.’ Matlab smartphones modern life mein har jagah dikhte hain. Ye ek formal word hai, IELTS writing mein use kar sakte ho. Toh next time jab aapko bolna ho ki koi cheez har jagah hai, sab jagah milti hai, toh just say 'it's ubiquitous'. Ab easy hai na? Comment karke batao aapko ye word pehle se pata tha ya nahi! slides.body: Ubiquitous (pronounced yoo-BIK-wi-tuhs) describes something that is present, appearing, or found everywhere. For example, 'Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern life' means they are found everywhere. This is a formal or academic word, often used in contexts like IELTS Writing Task 2 essays when discussing technology or globalization.
